title: docs(metadata-protocol): rollbackToPackageCommit docblock says each step records its revert commit; the record is best effort
body:
domain:skills#1 · os-project-manager · session_01FEkQ5pjSPT7ui2EUcunaVb

Filing gate: ① (a follow-up owed by work in flight). Contract review 6884842817 on PR #33465 (card #32504) found that the "revert commit is recorded" claim overstates what the code does, and sent the copy outside that diff to a follow-up.

## What is wrong

The `rollbackToPackageCommit` docblock in `packages/metadata-protocol/src/protocol.ts` (on main, just above `async rollbackToPackageCommit(request`) says each step "reverts the item's neighbours and records its revert commit". The record write is best effort. `recordPackageCommit` (`protocol-package-commit-record.ts`) catches every error, including an unprovisioned `sys_metadata_commit`, logs once at info (unprovisioned) or at error, and returns `null`. `revertCommit` then leaves `revertCommitId` out of its answer and returns normally. So a step that returns may have recorded nothing, and that revert is then on no package-commit timeline and cannot itself be reverted as a commit.

## Fix

Prose only, in that docblock: "attempts its own revert commit (best effort: when the commit store is unprovisioned or the write fails, nothing is recorded and the answer omits `revertCommitId`)". This matches the ADR-0067 amendment that PR #33465 adds. A `patch` changeset for `@objectstack/metadata-protocol` is owed, because TSDoc ships in the `.d.ts`.

## Out of scope

Whether `revertCommit` or `rollbackToPackageCommit` should become atomic is a maintainer decision. The ADR-0067 amendment's "What this amendment does not decide" section names it.

Blocked-by: #33465 (same ADR wording; land after it)
